key_insight: Odd-period supercells systematically suppress octahedral tilting and raise computed energies in high-entropy perovskite oxides.
engineering_relevance: Choosing tilt-compatible supercells can reduce structural and energetic bias in computational screening of perovskite oxides, including oxygen-vacancy predictions.
method: Used a machine-learning interatomic potential to study 13 high-entropy perovskite oxides.
Compared odd-period and tilt-commensurate supercells with configurational averaging.
Evaluated octahedral tilts, energies, and oxygen-vacancy formation energies.
evidence_signal: In approximately 1,700-atom cells, tilt differences persisted across all 13 compositions and energy differences persisted in most; odd-period cells also lowered vacancy formation energies in strongly tilted compositions.
watch_item: The abstract reports oxide simulation results, not solar-cell performance, and does not specify the proposed equimolar-supercell design rule.
paper_title: Supercell periodicity biases octahedral tilting and energetics in high-entropy perovskite oxides
